Voice AI Agents: a free, builder-level course from TechAurah on building voice agents: capture, VAD, endpointing, speech recognition, dialogue, synthesis, latency budgets, turn-taking, telephony constraints, consent and safety, cost per minute, and evaluation. 32 lessons in 10 modules, framework-free, Python standard library only, no API keys, no audio hardware. Speech components are deterministic local stand-ins driven by bundled fixtures (24 utterances, 12 scripted calls for the fictional BrightSmile Dental), so every number reproduces.

Key measured results: endpointing is 64.5 percent of the simulated latency ledger; fixed 400 ms and 800 ms endpointing each cut off all 3 slow fixture utterances while the adaptive policy cuts 1; committing to streaming partials at 60 percent of words scores 0.4135 WER against the batch final's 0.0702; phone numbers arrive exactly right 5 of 12 times unconfirmed and 12 of 12 with digit-level read-back correction; a domain-vocabulary post-processor makes WER worse (0.0702 to 0.0744) and is rejected in print. Capstone: a booking line graded against five gates fixed in writing on 2026-11-06 before the build; the as-built system passes 3 of 5 (success 0.5, p50 first audio 1251 ms), the hardened capstone passes 5 of 5 (success 1.0, 0 escapes, p50 742 ms, p95 891 ms, mean repairs 0.58, cost per successful booking 0.0581 USD at stated teaching rates).
